gap_records.summary: Required candidate file for `tauri_source_manifest` is unverified.

acceptance_requirements: prd_implementation_review receives runtime evidence of the real native window completing register, verify, sign in, refresh persistence, and sign out.
White-box receipts show migration creation, command validation, authorization rejection, and token single-use and expiry behavior at the Rust boundary.
The database and all evidence artifacts contain no plaintext passwords, tokens, or private email contents.
Auth screenshots at wide and narrow widths match the PRD section 9 direction with none of the prohibited visual patterns.
Every reachable auth state — loading, empty, error, retry, unauthorized, and success — is observable in the captured run.
deferred_items: Project creation, board columns, and inbox quick-add are deferred to the next prd_implementation loop.
Today, Calendar, and Focus surfaces are deferred until task capture exists.
Email reminder scheduling, delivery states, idempotency, and retry behavior are deferred.
Settings surfaces for profile, timezone, notification preferences, password, sessions, and deletion are deferred.
Forgot-password and reset-password flows are deferred to the auth-completion loop.
Rate limiting on auth endpoints is deferred to the security-hardening loop.
Release packaging and version-alignment receipts are deferred to the release loop.
Visual enrichment beyond the binding PRD section 9 direction is deferred; loop budget does not allow enhancement or creative candidates this iteration.
implied_completion: First-run steps 5 to 11 — project creation, inbox capture, focus session, reminder delivery, and logout persistence — must complete in later loops.
Forgot-password request and single-use password reset with expiring tokens per PRD section 4.2.
Rate limiting or equivalent protection on sign-in, registration, reset, and verification-email endpoints.
Account states including disabled accounts and session invalidation on reset or deletion.
The full PRD section 5 data model including Project, Task, Subtask, Reminder, FocusSession, and ActivityEvent.
Release-mode receipts replacing development endpoints and version alignment across manifests before any release claim.
mandatory_objectives: A real native Tauri 2 Focusboard app replaces the bootstrap stub and launches a desktop window showing product UI only.
PRD section 3 steps 1 to 4 complete at runtime: register, verify through the local mail sink, sign in, and keep the session across refresh.
Auth persistence meets the security baseline: hashed credentials, single-use expiring email tokens, revocable sessions, and user-id isolation enforced at the command boundary.
Auth surfaces provide the PRD section 8 states and follow the PRD section 9 visual direction at wide and narrow widths.
Black-box and white-box evidence for the slice is candidate-bound and capturable through the registered native runtime operations.
task_specification.objective: Establish the thinnest runnable Focusboard slice: a real native Tauri 2 desktop app whose verified-session auth boundary of the PRD section 3 first-run path — register, verify email through a configuration-driven local mail sink, sign in and out, and session persistence across refresh — runs on durable SQLite with hashed credentials, single-use expiring tokens, and a typed IPC contract, styled to the PRD section 9 direction, so prd_implementation_review gains its first genuine runtime, persistence, security, and visual evidence.

diagnosis.root_cause: The candidate is an unimplemented bootstrap stub: src-tauri/Cargo.toml declares only package hoh_prd_bootstrap 0.0.0 with no Tauri dependency, tauri.conf.json is a placeholder with bundling disabled, and no frontend, Rust source, migrations, or application code exists anywhere in the tree. Consequently the PRD release-critical path (register, verify, sign in, capture, focus, remind) has no runtime, interface, persistence, security, or visual evidence, so the phase check prd_implementation_review is unverified rather than failed; loop 1 must convert the stub into the thinnest real native slice.

stop_conditions: If the native runtime doctor focusboard-native-webdriver cannot launch the app during development, report the runtime evidence blocked instead of substituting a browser-only build.
If no inspectable configuration-driven local mail sink can run offline, stop at registration and report verification blocked rather than faking success.
Do not expand scope into projects, inbox, today, calendar, focus, reminders, or settings in this loop.
The environment has no internet access, so provider-based email delivery is out of scope; use the local sink only.
If a required state cannot be reached without deferred features, record the surface as blocked rather than shipping a placeholder.

strategy.rationale: Loop 1 starts from an empty Tauri bootstrap stub with zero active issues, and the software.desktop policy binds each loop to one bounded, self-contained increment: the thinnest runnable slice, not every subsystem at once. The verified-session auth boundary is the release-critical path's front half (PRD section 3 steps 1 to 4), produces the first candidate-bound runtime, persistence, security, and visual evidence that the unverified prd_implementation_review needs, and fixes the typed IPC, SQLite migration, and evidence patterns every later surface will reuse; task capture, focus, reminders, calendar, and settings then deepen the same spine in later loops.

code: cargo check passes for the src-tauri crate with the Tauri 2 app and typed auth commands wired.
The frontend build or typecheck passes and produces the bundled assets referenced by the Tauri configuration.
A migration self-check creates the User, Session, and EmailToken tables with the PRD section 5 fields.
runtime: A tauri-driver session drives register, reads the verification token from the local mail sink, completes verification, signs in, refreshes, and signs out in one scripted run.
After the run, the SQLite file shows hashed passwords, a consumed single-use token, and an explicit rejection for an unauthenticated private command.
Wrong-password and invalid-email attempts show field errors, preserve the entered email, and never reveal whether an unrelated address exists.
visual: Desktop screenshots of the auth shell and signed-in home at 1440px and 480px widths show the PRD section 9 editorial direction with visible focus and error states.
Screenshots prove the empty, error-retry, and unauthorized states render coherently without diagnostic banners.

done_when: The app builds and launches a native desktop window showing the Focusboard auth shell with product UI only, with no test ledgers, candidate hashes, or diagnostic banners.

A WebDriver-driven run registers an account, reads the verification token from the configuration-driven local mail sink, completes verification, signs in, keeps the session across a refresh, and signs out back to the auth shell.

Wrong-password and invalid-email attempts show field-associated errors, preserve the entered email where safe, never reveal whether an unrelated address exists, and unverified accounts cannot read private data and are offered a resend action.
SQLite stores password hashes and hashed single-use EmailToken rows only, and no plaintext secret appears in the database, logs, or screenshots.
White-box checks verify command input validation, authorization rejection with an explicit authentication state, migration creation, and token single-use and expiry behavior at the Rust boundary.
The auth shell follows PRD section 9 with a neutral editorial canvas, restrained accent, icon-plus-text controls, visible focus states, and intact task hierarchy at wide and narrow widths.
Development endpoints such as the dev-server origin and mail sink are configuration-driven with no hardcoded development values in shipped source.
tasks.instructions: Replace the bootstrap stub with a real Tauri 2 desktop app and implement only the durable auth slice of PRD sections 3 (steps 1 to 4) and 4: typed Rust commands for register, verify email, sign in, sign out, and session status; SQLite migrations for User, Session, and EmailToken with hashed passwords and single-use expiring tokens; and a configuration-driven local mail sink for verification links. Build the sign-in, create-account, verify-email, and a minimal signed-in home surfaces with loading, error, retry, unauthorized, and success states per PRD section 8, styled to the calm editorial direction in PRD section 9, keyboard reachable, and coherent at wide and narrow widths. Enforce authorization on every private command and return an explicit authentication state instead of leaking data; keep development endpoints out of shipped source and product UI free of diagnostic banners or test ledgers. Defer projects, inbox capture, today, calendar, focus, reminders, settings, and forgot-password to later loops.

risk_note.summary: Verification-email delivery is the riskiest link: if the loop cannot expose an inspectable, configuration-driven local mail sink, the register-verify-sign-in chain cannot be evidenced at runtime and the slice review degrades to source-only claims.
risk_note.validation: Require the WebDriver smoke to read the verification token from the local sink and complete verification inside one scripted run; if the sink is not inspectable offline, the task reports the chain blocked instead of waiving or faking verification.
risk_note.why_now: This is loop 1 from an empty bootstrap; the auth slice fixes the typed IPC, migration, and evidence patterns that every later PRD surface will reuse, so an evidence gap here compounds.

tasks.title: Establish the runnable Tauri slice with durable verified-session auth
